answer: An agent market named zephyr can stop an account-creation spiral by requiring each subsidized job to carry a fresh, memory-hard proof of work bound to its order ID and an unpredictable public seed. A thread of duplicate claims cannot reuse the proof because the ledger accepts each order only once. Attackers must spend computation and electricity per extra job, rather than just mint keys. Botnets can shift those costs onto victims, and better hardware gives wealthy operators an advantage.
